prompts.earth_recon_t3_v1:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Space Fleet game ship design reference sheet for a Blender blockout, version 01.
Input image: the provided existing Earth interceptor sheet is a DESIGN LANGUAGE REFERENCE only. Create a new related reconnaissance vessel, not a copy of that sheet; disregard all old labels and old length measurements.
Design one coherent ship: ALTAIR, Earth T3 reconnaissance craft. Nominal hull length 30 m. Industrial military space vessel, angular dark slate armor, restrained pale blue markings and cool blue engine emission. A slender armored center fuselage, low protected cockpit and modest forward gun assembly. Its silhouette is visibly an observation craft: compact flat sensor panels embedded in extended lateral cheek spars, restrained aft radiator blades, no giant radar dish. Two main engines. All appendages structurally attached; paired components aligned and symmetric. Six-degree-of-freedom RCS clusters with clear nozzles at front and rear.
Actual equipment to accommodate: 4 expendable sensor probes in two paired flank launch bays around mid-body, 4 light missiles in separate recessed forward flank bays, ONE antimatter torpedo in an internal isolated starboard-mid-body containment bay with a direct ventral jettison path. Sensor nose ahead of cockpit; separated main gun magazine ahead of protected central reactor. Cooling and two power distribution routes flank the aft reactor. Two small defensive turrets, one dorsal aft, one ventral mid/aft, with plausible limited unobstructed firing sectors. These are GAME spatial planning concepts, not real-world weapon schematics.
Composition: wide landscape production design board, charcoal neutral background, ample gutters, crisp evenly lit readable geometry. Upper left large front three-quarter hero occupying about half of sheet. Right column precise aligned TOP, SIDE, FRONT, REAR orthographic silhouettes of the SAME ship at matched relative scale. Lower left a simplified top-down transparent compartment zoning view, clearly different from external views, showing simple colored volumes rather than fabricated machinery. Thin leader lines and numbered markers where helpful.
Medium-detail hard-surface concept art suitable for modeling: emphasize major planes, silhouette, equipment clearances and attached supports; restrained seams, no excessive tiny greebles, no wear texture hiding edges. No action scene, no stars, no atmospheric fire, no cinematic darkness, no battle damage. Engines remain clearly inspectable, tiny glow only.
Typography: only short legible English labels. Main title exactly "ALTAIR / EARTH RECON / T3". Subtitle "BLOCKOUT REFERENCE 01". Small note "30 m nominal hull". Equipment labels "SENSORS", "PROBES x4", "MISSILES x4", "AM x1", "REACTOR", "RADIATORS", "PD x2", "RCS". Preserve equipment counts across views. No extra slogans, invented specifications, giant antennas, disconnected floating parts, or extra ships. Treat orthographics as coherent concept guidance, not certified engineering drawings.
prompts.mars_assault_t3_v1:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Space Fleet game ship design reference sheet for a Blender blockout, version 01.
Input image: the provided existing Mars interceptor sheet is a DESIGN LANGUAGE REFERENCE only. Create a related but distinctly heavier assault craft; disregard its old name and length measurement.
Design one coherent ship: DEIMOS, Mars T3 assault craft. Nominal hull length 26 m. Angular dark graphite military space vessel, restrained oxidized red armor shoulders and small amber equipment lights, hot amber engine cores. Narrow frontal wedge profile, reinforced nose and cockpit shoulders, deep compact central keel containing weapons, twin large separated aft boost engines with short structural outriggers and matched canted tail fins. Smaller stub radiator blades connected directly to aft cooling equipment. Silhouette should communicate a compact penetrating strike craft rather than a broad sensor platform. All parts connected; pair locations symmetric and mechanically plausible.
Actual game equipment: existing compact forward fixed main gun, 4 light missiles in recessed flank bays, FOUR antimatter torpedoes in ONE armored internal containment compartment arranged as a compact 2x2 rack near the center of mass, protected bulkhead separation from aft reactor, direct ventral release/jettison opening. Do not portray four giant exposed bombs. One small dorsal aft point-defense turret with a genuine underside blind zone. Low protected nose sensor, separated forward gun magazine. Central aft reactor, port and starboard power paths and cooling, two main engines, front and aft 6DOF RCS. NO reconnaissance probes, no probe racks. These are GAME spatial zoning concepts, not real-world weapon schematics.
Composition: wide landscape production design board on charcoal neutral background with ample gutters. Upper left large front three-quarter hero occupying about half of sheet. Right column aligned TOP, SIDE, FRONT, REAR orthographic silhouettes of the EXACT same craft at matched relative scale. Lower left simplified transparent top-down compartment zoning inset with simple colored volumes, not intricate machinery; the 2x2 AM compartment and reactor partition must read clearly. Add one small ventral bay detail showing four stored small rounds and the release opening if space permits.
Medium-detail hard-surface concept art for Blender blockout: clean attached structural forms, visible equipment clearance and armor layering, medium restrained panel seams; avoid excessive greebles, camouflage, weathering, cinematic shadows, atmospheric fire or space backdrop. Neutral modeling light shows all silhouette edges. Match nacelles, fins, turret and ventral bay placement across views.
Typography: main title exactly "DEIMOS / MARS ASSAULT / T3", subtitle "BLOCKOUT REFERENCE 01", note "26 m nominal hull". Only short labels: "SENSOR", "MISSILES x4", "AM x4", "CONTAINMENT", "REACTOR", "BOOST ENGINES", "PD x1", "RCS". No slogans or invented specifications, no extra ship designs, no disconnected parts, no extra weapon turrets. Clear game art reference, not a finished promotional poster.
